lane: Backend/AI: Trò chuyện với tri thức, Lô 2 backend (model tiers, 300 s wait, streaming, memory) plus the prompt-assembler part of Lô 0/1 (knowledge brief layer, method pack fix)
goal: Persona chat gets per-persona model tiers (standard 'Thường' and deep_knowledge 'Tri thức sâu', each with primary and fallback model, reasoning, output ceiling, total wait and per-message budget), Admin-configurable through a versioned ai_persona_model_tiers table read like ai_context_configs; an opt-in SSE streaming mode in ai-persona-chat (meta, delta, done, error) whose done payload equals today's JSON; a bundled knowledge-brief layer in the prompt assembler generated from packages/content/data/knowledge-briefs; longer replies and 12 x 2,500 memory for the deep tier only; and the communication-mentor method pack fix. Code and an unapplied migration only.
successCriteria: With no tier row in the database and a standard-tier persona, the model route, deadline, cost cap, history (8 x 800), prompt text and non-stream JSON are identical to today.

The 5 book personas (book-strategic-thinker, book-harmony-guide, book-stoic-journal, book-dhammapada, book-i-ching) resolve to deep_knowledge by default; the tier builds a 2-step chain with reasoning on, a raised maxTokens, its own total deadline and cost cap.

The tier total wait is capped by the platform wall clock (Free plan 150 s => 135 s usable; paid 400 s => up to 300 s) and the non-stream path never exceeds 140 s, so a request never outlives the Edge limits; the cap is reported, not hidden.

stream:true (or Accept: text/event-stream) returns text/event-stream with meta first, delta chunks, heartbeats, and exactly one done (same JSON body as non-stream) or one error; pre-model failures (auth, body, switch, quota) keep their JSON status codes; crisis replies never call a model.

If the primary model fails before any delta is sent the fallback runs; after deltas were sent the turn ends with error stream_interrupted and no fallback; usage_events is written once per turn in both modes.
Output safety runs on the accumulated streamed text; a hit stops the stream and done carries the safety replacement with moderationStatus blocked.

When a knowledge brief exists for the persona it is injected as its own layer after the persona skill; Admin-published persona skill still wins over the repo default skill; a missing brief falls back to today's prompt.

Knowledge-tier output contract drops the 'concise / one reflective question' rule (150-300 words default, cite a part of the book only when sure, question optional); other personas keep it; safety and transparency layer stays first and unchanged.
communication-mentor gets relationship_boundaries; every other persona keeps its method pack.
Deno tests for tiers, SSE framing, fallback before first delta, brief injection and the method pack pass; validate:backend, supabase:check, migration-ledger check and prompt:consumers:check pass.

impact.entryPoint: Chat with a persona in the app (old builds: JSON; new builds: stream:true). Admin later: a 'Hạng model' page calling get/save/publish RPCs.
impact.dataWrite: New table ai_persona_model_tiers (versioned draft/active/archived, service-role read only, RPC writes audited). chat_messages, chat_sessions and usage_events writes unchanged in shape; usage metadata gains tier, knowledgeBrief and stream fields.
impact.backendContract: ai-persona-chat accepts optional stream:true; SSE events meta/delta/done/error; done.data equals the non-stream JSON plus promptStack.knowledgeBriefId/Version and modelTier (additive). Request body limit for this function rises from 32 KB to 64 KB for the longer deep-tier history.
impact.adminVisibility: Traces and usage_events carry modelTier, tierSource, knowledgeBriefId, stream and streamOutcome; Admin can publish tier configs through RPCs (UI pending).
impact.privacySafety: Same data sent to the same ZDR/deny OpenRouter routes; crisis check before any model call; output check on accumulated stream text; knowledge briefs are Nilaza-written repo text, no user data. Longer history (deep tier only) sends more of the user's own recent turns to the model.
impact.observability: Root span metadata includes tier and stream; per-step spans unchanged; cost tally covers streamed calls from the final usage chunk.
impact.rollback: Clients without stream:true are unaffected. Publishing a tier config that maps every persona to standard restores today's behaviour; revert the code and redeploy ai-persona-chat; the table can stay unused.

skillReview.evidence: Safety block never falls through; output check inside the router path; ZDR/deny kept; every model call keeps sign-in, switch and quota; total attempts sized against the Edge limits (now via streaming and the plan wall clock).

dependencyReview.evidence: Supabase Edge Function limits and OpenRouter streaming format from official docs below, checked 2026-11-25. No package added.

externalSourceReview.reason: Wall clock: Free 150 s, paid plans 400 s; request idle timeout 150 s (504 if no response is sent before it); CPU 2 s; memory 256 MB. Singapore project is on the Free plan (docs/HANDOFF_CURRENT_STATE.vi.md), so 300 s is not reachable until a paid plan.

stream:true; SSE data lines; ': OPENROUTER PROCESSING' comments must be skipped; chat completions send usage in a final chunk before [DONE]; mid-stream errors arrive as a chunk with a top-level error and finish_reason error with HTTP 200; aborting the connection cancels billing on supported providers.

securityReview.authzRls: ai_persona_model_tiers has RLS on, no policies, service_role select only; RPCs check has_capability (ai.read / ai.manage, editors draft only) and are audited, like ai_context_configs.
securityReview.sensitiveData: No new data class: the same message, history and data block go to the same ZDR/deny routes. Deep tier keeps up to 12 x 2,500 characters of the user's own history (was 8 x 800). Knowledge briefs are repo text.
securityReview.secretsLogging: Only the presence/value path of OPENROUTER_API_KEY already used by the provider; no new secret; .env not read; stream events carry no keys or prompts.
securityReview.externalInput: stream flag is a strict boolean; tier config from the database is clamped field by field and unknown keys ignored; persona id/slug from the client only selects a tier (bounded by the tier cost cap and the unchanged daily quota); brief text is repo-controlled and generated, never from requests.
securityReview.dependencies: No package added or upgraded; Deno std and supabase-js imports unchanged.
securityReview.migrationRelease: Migration 20261125090000 is written, not applied; ai-persona-chat deploy needs Owner approval; without the migration the function reads no row and uses code defaults.
securityReview.stopCondition: Stop if the standard path stops being byte-identical in prompt or route, if safety checks can be skipped in stream mode, or if Deno tests fail and cannot be fixed inside the write scope.

managerTestPath: After the Owner applies migration 20261125090000 and deploys ai-persona-chat: an old app build chatting with Aristotle gets the same short reply as before. A new build chatting with Chiến Lược Gia Cổ Điển sees text appear progressively, a longer answer (about 150-300 words) that may not end with a question, and the reply is saved in history. Turning the network off mid-answer shows an error, not a half answer saved as final.
residualRisk: Streaming through the Supabase gateway and the mobile fetch stack is not verified on a device or deployed function. 300 s is only reachable on a paid Supabase plan; on Free the deep tier waits at most 135 s. Whether the runtime keeps running persistence after the client disconnects mid-stream is not verified. Admin UI for tiers is not built. Deep-tier quality and cost need a blind eval before release.
